item: Democrats won the Texas governorship; Abbott had paused new rural AI data centres. Texas was due to host about a quarter of new US data-centre capacity by 2030.
note: Inference: power/permitting risk for grid-dependent leveraged builders; raises the value of on-site power (gas turbines, microreactors).

item: US midterms: Democrats won House (~255) and Senate (~55). Nasdaq-100 futures -2%, Nikkei ~-4% on the night.
A Democratic Senate makes extension of expiring OBBB tax cuts (from late 2028) less likely.

NVIDIA reportedly told data-centre partners (verbally) that at least 51% of revenue must come from non-China clients; also reports about Jensen Huang's ties to a person linked to Chinese intelligence.
Saudi Aramco Q3 profit +35% on high oil prices while Saudi GDP shrank 3.8%; plot against Syria's Homs refinery foiled.
US ammonia imports from Trinidad down 34%, adding to fertiliser inflation.
Trump says $4bn/yr military aid to Israel will wind down by year-end, earlier than the 2028 expiry.
Iran's energy-squeeze strategy: US gasoline above $4, diesel above $6. Democrats can cut Pentagon funding to pressure an end to the Iran war.
note: Bears on H2 kill signal K2 (Hormuz/Iran deal collapsing diesel prices).

item: Trump 2.0 pivoting to stabilise US-China ties: trade-truce renewals, flexibility on chip controls, 'transactional' noises on Taiwan.
Trump may push Ukraine toward land-for-peace; possible Xi/Putin meetings at APEC; US pushing Europe to fund US arms for Ukraine (PURL).
note: Inference: tilts defense spending toward Europe/NATO.

item: Indonesia: Prabowo deployed 20,000+ troops to Jakarta after arresting aides; 'market jitters'.
US claimed strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz; Vance says a deal 'could be close'; US fuel prices at records.
Hackers sabotaged supermarket refrigeration in six European countries; Russia suspected, possibly testing NATO Article 5.
Belgium near government collapse over an $11bn budget gap; debt >108% of GDP; borrowing costs at 15-year highs.
GMO Internet Group (9449.T) ransomware hit its cloud/forex platform; its 2031 bond spreads widened 50bp.
Direct Ukraine-Russia talks confirmed for Abu Dhabi next week; Trump may want a deal at APEC or G20.
ISW: Russia lost net territory in Ukraine for a second month; Ukraine claims a record 54,000 Russian casualties.
Xi's purges leave the Central Military Commission with two members; 71 senior officials under investigation in nine months; fourth term expected at the 2027 Party Congress.
Turkey detained 85 members of a network linked to Russian arson at a Starlink ground station in Poland.
Speculation Netanyahu (caretaker PM) could join US in resuming strikes on Iran; Cambodia cruise costs jumped after Hormuz squeeze.
Houthis claimed another hit on Saudi Ras Tanura refinery; crude +1.62%.
Woodside selling its 33% Greater Sunrise gas stake to Timor-Leste's state firm.

Indonesia: Prabowo deployed 20,000 troops to Jakarta after investigators say his chief of staff (ex-police chief Listyo) ran unauthorised surveillance on him. The rupiah is at record lows, the central bank governor quit early in July, and MSCI has threatened a downgrade over the opaque equity market.
note: Inference: rising EM/SE Asia risk premium; the Iran-war energy shock is hitting importers.

item: Trump after hosting Putin's envoy: a 'big agreement' coming that 'might involve all of Europe'; Russia-Ukraine talks resume in Abu Dhabi next week.
note: Inference: a ceasefire would change the defense-tech demand story (Anduril, GA, drones).

item: 21+ flights across Europe got fake bomb threats on Thursday, the third day of hoaxes this week.
Leaked documents show Russia plans to supply Iran with 90 helicopter-mounted LMUR missile launchers.
note: Inference: points to a longer Iran war, so oil and diesel stay high; works against H2's Hormuz/Iran-deal kill signal.

item: South Korea is expanding naval operations toward Hormuz and Somalia (anti-piracy, mine clearing). The Iran war has drained Western naval capacity and Somali piracy is filling the gap; Korea imports nearly all its oil.

France: 600k-1.5m on strike over wages and the cost of living, six months before elections Le Pen is forecast to win; Paris must choose between concessions that worsen its fiscal crisis and growing protests.
note: Inference: adds to European sovereign stress (with Belgium, Nov 3).

item: Paraguay: President Peña resigned after the collapse of digital bank Ueno (about 10% of the state pension fund's portfolio); he had resisted pressure to drop recognition of Taiwan.
note: Inference: small risk to one of Taiwan's few diplomatic allies.

item: Jensen Huang apologised for an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a Singapore-based exec US intelligence says works for China's MSS. She worked for Megaspeed, which bought $4.8bn of advanced chips via Southeast Asian affiliates and which US officials call an MSS front. Nvidia's board says there's no reason to believe secrets were compromised and has opened an independent investigation; Trump called Huang 'an honourable guy'.
note: Data: NVDA pre-market $177.75 on 2026-11-09, -4.8% vs the $186.64 close (yfinance). Inference: key-person and governance risk at the compute leader.

item: The newsletter expects Washington hawks to push for tighter chip controls: closing the Southeast Asia re-export loophole and treating key AI firms more like defense contractors (counter-intel briefings, disclosure rules). A short-seller flagged the ties in May.
note: Inference: reverses the easing trend noted Nov 5; China is Nvidia's second-largest market.

item: After the midterm loss Trump replaced chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller.
note: Inference: less bipartisan compromise ahead of two years of House oversight; more domestic, less deal-making abroad.

item: China and Gabon elevated ties, signing pacts on security, trade and mining that secure priority access to Gabon's manganese (an EV battery input).
The lead piece also cites Elon Musk's Starlink throttling and Anthropic's collapsed Pentagon negotiations as examples of tech leaders holding outsized geopolitical power.

Jensen Huang and Nvidia face a shareholder class action alleging they concealed his ties to Megaspeed, the Singapore firm alleged to have smuggled chips to China; reports also claim Nvidia may have intervened in a US probe of Megaspeed (Reuters, 2026-11-09).
note: Data: NVDA closed $178.67 on 2026-11-09, -4.3% vs $186.64 on Nov 6 and -10.7% vs $200.13 on Nov 4 (yfinance). Inference: litigation adds to key-person risk ahead of Nov 17 earnings.

item: Trump said the military part of the Iran war is 'effectively over' after meeting Qatar's PM; Rubio says no breakthrough is near. Brent fell 1.7% to $90.99 per the newsletter.
note: Data: Brent futures $91.31 on 2026-11-10 vs $98.32 on Nov 6, about -7% (yfinance BZ=F). Relevant to H2.K2 (Hormuz reopening / Iran deal collapses diesel and inflation expectations).

item: ECB President Lagarde leaves in Feb 2027, early, to lock in technocratic leadership before 2027 elections. Two-man race: Klaas Knot (slightly more hawkish, economists' frontrunner) and Pablo Hernandez de Cos (BIS). EU leaders aim to decide by Christmas.
note: Inference: Le Pen, now favourite for France, has called on the ECB to buy French debt; a euro-sceptic win would pressure EU bond markets and add to global long-end yield stress.

item: ExxonMobil signed a preliminary deal with Venezuela's interim government to explore drilling, months after calling the country 'uninvestable'.
GAO: about 17,000 F-35 parts worth ~$1.3bn are missing from the Pentagon's logistics database.
US, Russian and Ukrainian delegates resume peace talks in Abu Dhabi; reports say Washington asked whether Russia would accept a NATO-like Western guarantee for Ukraine.
France blamed Iran's Revolutionary Guards for last month's cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration systems and issued arrest warrants for the Shahid Kaveh cyber unit.

Deep dive on Alice Huang and Megaspeed: an obscure gaming subsidiary (7Road International) rebranded as Megaspeed, got 'Nvidia Cloud Partner' status within months and bought $5-7bn (140-240k) of restricted H100/H200 chips. Commerce found ~50,000 chips unaccounted for. Ownership moved to Swiftdata, a new Singapore entity, letting Nvidia tell Washington there was no Chinese equity. Singapore confirms it is investigating Megaspeed. Huang has vanished.
note: Data: NVDA closed $168.89 on 2026-11-10, -5.5% on the day and -15.6% vs $200.13 on Nov 4 (yfinance). Inference: the questions now reach Nvidia's own partner vetting, not just Huang's private life.

item: Singapore filings suggest Alibaba was Megaspeed's lead financier and anchor client; chips were routed via server farms used by Chinese tech giants including Alibaba.
note: Data: BABA closed $102.72 on 2026-11-10 vs $109.45 on Nov 6, -6.1% (yfinance). Alibaba is not in the tracker universe.

item: China's trade surplus passed $1T in the first ten months of 2026, on track to beat the 2025 full-year record of $1.2T (CNBC).
note: Inference: supports more tariff and export-control pressure from trading partners.

item: World Bank projects an 800m job shortfall in developing countries over 15 years: 1.2bn young people entering, ~400m jobs on track.
House Republicans blocked Massie's impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Hegseth (abuse of power, unauthorised Iran war).
Abu Dhabi US-Russia-Ukraine talks: Zelensky calls day one 'constructive'; the newsletter expects at most a prisoner swap.
Syria weighs sending special forces to help Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, after a $400m Saudi loan.
XPeng two-seat flying cars could launch in China as soon as next summer (Guardian).
